verdict.rationale: Cactus documents its own path to task-specialized models. You generate tool-calling training data from your tools and a product description (POST /generations, /tool_schemas), then fine-tune Needle 3 locally with LoRA or on hosted GPUs and download the result. The Python package also lets you define tools by decorating functions. This is a developer-oriented model-specialization workflow rather than an assistant builder with personas or instructions. Hands-on reports show a fine-tuned Needle 3 scored low on a tool-calling benchmark, and users note it must match the use case closely. Missing for 10: a first-class configurable 'assistant' abstraction (persona/system instructions, saved assistants), a non-developer creation flow, and independent evidence that the specialized models perform reliably.
